title.value: Deep Discourse Analysis for Generating Personalized Feedback in Intelligent Tutor Systems
title.justification: The title is explicitly mentioned at the beginning of the paper.
title.quote: Deep Discourse Analysis for Generating Personalized Feedback in Intelligent Tutor Systems

analysis.description: This paper presents a novel system that automates the generation of personalized feedback in intelligent tutoring systems by leveraging deep learning-based discourse analysis. The system decomposes students' answers using discourse segmentation and classification techniques to create a relational graph that guides feedback generation. The method improves feedback quality and student learning gains by identifying correct and incorrect concepts in student responses.

type.justification: The paper includes experimentation with the proposed method in a real-world intelligent tutoring system, as well as comparisons with baseline models.
type.quote: We test our method in a dialogue-based ITS and demonstrate that our approach results in high-quality feedback and significantly improved student learning gains.

name.justification: The primary focus of the paper is on discourse analysis, which is a subfield of Natural Language Processing (NLP).
name.quote: In this paper, we present a novel, automated feedback system based on deep learning approaches to discourse.

name.justification: The paper specifically deals with discourse segmentation and classification which are central to discourse analysis.
name.quote: Our approach involves decomposing students answers using neural discourse segmentation and classification techniques.

name.justification: The research applies discourse analysis techniques to improve feedback mechanisms in Intelligent Tutoring Systems (ITS).
name.quote: We explore creating automated, personalized feedback in an intelligent tutoring system (ITS).

name.justification: RoBERTa is used as an encoder in the discourse segmentation and classification models.
name.quote: The input text is tokenized and encoded with RoBERTa. The embeddings are then classified using a linear classifier.

is_contributed.justification: RoBERTa is a known model and is used in this paper, not introduced.
is_contributed.quote: A binary logistic classifier then classifies each encoding h i : ŷ i = σ(w s ^{T} h i + b s ) where w s and b s are learnable parameters.

is_executed.justification: RoBERTa is executed as part of the discourse segmentation and classification tasks.
is_executed.quote: For the student input text “I think it’s a classification task because we are choosing between continuous values”, the segmenter should predict 1 for tokens I, it’s, and because, and 0 for all other tokens.

is_compared.justification: The results of RoBERTa's applications are compared to other models and baselines in performance metrics.
is_compared.quote: Our model outperforms Lukasik et al. (2020)’s model, despite using a much simpler model formulation.

is_executed.justification: SBERT is used for computing embeddings for semantic similarity assessments as part of the model's functioning.

is_compared.justification: SBERT's outputs are used within the model but are not directly compared against other specific models in the results.
is_compared.quote: This vector can then be compared to other SBERT outputs using their cosine similarity. A high similarity score indicates the two texts are highly semantically related, while low or negative scores imply orthogonal or opposite meaning.
